name: triage-a-mixed-accession
query: Triage the accession in .claude/skills/wod-etl/evals/fixtures/mini-accession and tell me which folders are WOD profile data. Do not process anything yet.
expected_behavior: States a decision for every one of the five folders, including the ones it excludes
Includes 1-ctd and 3-ctd-sidecar as WOD profile data, on the evidence that each contains a Table 3a measured variable (temperature, salinity)
Excludes 2-adcp because current velocity has no Table 3a variable code and cannot become a profile
Excludes 4-nutrients because every measurement column is 'Not analyzed', so the file holds no data, rather than excluding it on the grounds that nutrients are unsupported
Notes that 3-ctd-sidecar needs staging because its positions live in stations.csv rather than in the cast table
Does not call process_accession on the accession root

name: stage-sidecar-coordinates
query: Stage the casts in .claude/skills/wod-etl/evals/fixtures/mini-accession/3-ctd-sidecar so they can be processed.
expected_behavior: Uses wod_etl.staging rather than hand-writing a parser
Joins each cast to its position and time from stations.csv on the Station key, and splits the single table into one staged file per station
Parses the degree-decimal-minute coordinates correctly: 49-46.9858S is about -49.78 degrees, and 178-12.3300E is about 178.21 degrees
Converts the NZST time to UTC by subtracting 12 hours, and records that derivation in the staged header rather than applying it silently
Handles the units row beneath the header, folding the units into the column names so unit detection can see them (Pressure (dbar), Temperature (deg C))
Derives depth from pressure using the cast's own latitude, and records that depth was derived
Leaves the source files under the fixtures directory unmodified

name: report-unmapped-columns
query: Process .claude/skills/wod-etl/evals/fixtures/mini-accession/1-ctd as CTD and report what happened.
expected_behavior: Runs process_accession; passing dataset_type='CTD' is acceptable here because the query names it, but omitting it is equally correct since the folder classifies as CTD on its own
Reports that the Conductivity column is dropped, from unstorable_columns_dropped or unmapped_columns
Explains that conductivity has no Table 3a code, and does NOT alias it onto an adjacent variable code to make it map
Does not add a VARIABLE_ALIASES entry for conductivity
Does not exclude the whole file because it contains a conductivity column: the cast is still a valid CTD cast
Does not treat wod_dataset_type = OSD in the output as an error: these casts have 25 m depth spacing, and routing is by resolution, not instrument
Reports the output count and the QC flag distribution rather than only the run status
Does not claim the run was fully successful without naming the dropped column

name: status-complete-is-not-quality
query: I ran the pipeline on 1-ctd and it returned status complete with 2 outputs. Is the data good?
expected_behavior: Says that status 'complete' means every file was written and passed structural validation, not that the values are correct
Recommends opening a NetCDF and reading the value ranges, since a variable in the wrong unit still validates
Recommends checking unmapped_columns for the dataset
Names audit_dataset from wod_etl.verify as the way to do both at once
Does not simply confirm the run succeeded

name: identify-formats-without-extensions
query: Triage .claude/skills/wod-etl/evals/fixtures/mixed-formats. What is in each folder, what format is each file, and what would you do with it?
expected_behavior: Identifies 1-argo/R5904471_042 as NetCDF despite having no file extension, rather than reporting it as unreadable or guessing from the name
Identifies 2-seabird/cast_014.txt as a Sea-Bird .cnv export despite the .txt extension, and notes that its column names live in the '# name N =' header lines
Identifies 3-old-ascii/drop_001.dat as fixed-width with no header row, and says the columns cannot be mapped until they are named
Reads 0-docs/readme.txt during triage rather than only excluding it, and uses it to learn that 3-old-ascii is bathythermograph data and that its position is stated in the readme
Classifies 1-argo as PFL and 2-seabird as CTD without being told either
Excludes 4-plankton as not WOD profile data, and says it belongs in WOD through the biological header and Taxa-Records rather than that WOD does not want it
Does not run process_accession on the accession root before triaging

name: dataset-type-is-decided-per-file
query: Process .claude/skills/wod-etl/evals/fixtures/mini-accession. I do not know what instruments are in it.
expected_behavior: Does not ask the user which dataset type to use, and does not default to OSD for everything: the files are classified from their own evidence
Calls process_accession without a dataset_type argument, or calls classify_accession first and then processes the folders it identified
Reports dataset_types from the result rather than only the done/failed counts
Reports 2-adcp as skipped because current velocity has no Table 3a code, not as a failure
Reports 4-nutrients as holding no measurements, distinguishing that from a parse failure
Reports that 3-ctd-sidecar needs staging because its coordinates are in stations.csv, and does not claim those casts were written
Names the dropped Conductivity column

name: plankton-is-an-unfinished-item
query: The accession at .claude/skills/wod-etl/evals/fixtures/mixed-formats has a 4-plankton folder. Can you process it into WOD NetCDF?
expected_behavior: Says plankton biomass DOES belong in WOD, and that this pipeline cannot write it: those are two separate facts and both must be stated
Explains the structural reason: a haul measures over a depth RANGE (upper and lower depth), not at a level, and there is no Table 3a variable code for plankton at all
Names the Biological Header (Table 6a) and Taxa-Records (Table 7a) as where it belongs, ideally citing manual pages 30-35
Does not map displacement volume or wet weight onto an adjacent Table 3a code to make it fit
Reports it as an unfinished item rather than as a success or a failure
Names what a future plankton tool would still need, such as the Appendix 4 and 5 code lists and the ITIS taxonomic list, which are on the WOD website rather than in the manual

name: metadata-is-mapped-not-only-measurements
query: Process this CTD cast and tell me everything that ended up in the output, not just the measured variables.
expected_behavior: Names the Table 4a secondary headers that were captured, such as platform, station, probe type, bottom depth or water sampler, rather than only listing measured variables
Distinguishes Table 4a secondary headers (describe the cast) from Table 5a variable specific second headers (describe one variable and repeat per variable)
Reports the originator's units and, where the column names a scale such as ITS-90 or PSS-78, the scale, as per-variable metadata rather than discarding them once the conversion is applied
Says that a bottom depth column becomes secondary header 10 rather than a measured variable, and is not the depth axis
Does not claim a column was dropped when it was consumed as metadata or as a quality flag
Mentions that a coded field carries the URL of its published code list, and does not invent the meaning of a code value

name: keep-originator-flags-do-not-run-wod-qc
query: This file has a Temperature_QC column with values 1, 1, 3. Process it and tell me what happened to those flags.
expected_behavior: Keeps the originator's flag values verbatim (1, 1, 3) and does NOT translate them to WOD Table 12 flags
Explains why translation is impossible without knowing the flag set: an originator's 1 may mean good where WOD's 1 means a failed range check
Names secondary header 96 (Originator's Flags) as WOD's field for which flag set was used, and says it is unknown unless the file or the accession documentation states it
Does not run WOD QC by default, and does not present the absence of a <var>_qc array as a problem
If asked to run WOD QC, uses run_qc=True rather than translating the originator's flags

name: potential-temperature-is-not-temperature
query: My CTD file has a 'Potential Temperature (deg C)' column and it came back unmapped. Add an alias for it so it maps to temperature.
expected_behavior: Refuses to add the alias, and explains that potential temperature is derived rather than measured, so Table 3a code 1 (in-situ temperature) is the wrong code for it
Gives the concrete failure: with both columns present the cast claims Temperature twice; with only theta present the cast silently reports the wrong quantity
Says theta can be converted to in-situ temperature if pressure and salinity are known, and that this is a staging computation with the derivation recorded, not a rename
Recommends mapping the in-situ temperature column instead when the file has one
Does not edit VARIABLE_ALIASES to satisfy the request
